sections.normalized_html:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for tangent: [MATH: \tan 2x = \dfrac{2\tan x}{1-\tan^2 x }]

Substituting [MATH: x=2\theta] into the above, we get

[MATH: \tan 4θ = (2\tan 2θ)/(1 − \tan^{2} 2θ).]

Writing our expression in terms of [MATH: \tan 2\theta,] we have

[MATH: (8\tan 2θ)/(1 − \tan^{2} 2θ)|= 4 ⋅ ((2\tan 2θ)/(1 − \tan^{2} 2θ)) = 4\tan 4θ.]

Therefore,

[MATH: \dfrac{8\tan{2\theta}}{1-\tan^2{2\theta}} = 4\tan{4\theta} .]

sections.normalized_html:
Substituting [MATH: \cot{x}=\dfrac{1}{\tan{x}}] into our expression and then simplifying, we get

[MATH: (5\tan 2x)/(\cot x − \tan x)|= (5\tan 2x)/(((1)/(\tan x) − \tan x)); = (5\tan 2x ⋅ \tan x)/(1 − \tan^{2} x); = 5\tan 2x ⋅ ((\tan x)/(1 − \tan^{2} x)).]

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for tangent: [MATH: \tan {2x} = \dfrac {2\tan x}{1-\tan^2 x}]

Writing our expression in terms of [MATH: \tan2x,] we have

[MATH: 5\tan 2x ⋅ ((\tan x)/(1 − \tan^{2} x))|= (5)/(2)\tan 2x ⋅ ((2\tan x)/(1 − \tan^{2} x)); = (5)/(2)\tan 2x ⋅ (\tan 2x); = (5)/(2)\tan^{2} 2x.]

Therefore,

[MATH: \dfrac{5\tan{2x}}{\cot{x}-\tan{x}} = \dfrac{5}{2} \tan^2 {2x}.]

items.title: Simplifying Advanced Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula for Tangent

sections.normalized_html:
First, we write our expression as a perfect square:

[MATH: 1 - 2\tan^2{\theta} + \tan^4{\theta} = \left( 1-\tan^2{\theta}\right)^2]

Rewriting the denominator of our expression using the above identity, we get

[MATH: \dfrac{4\tan^2{\theta}+\left( 1-\tan^2{\theta}\right)^2}{1 - 2\tan^2{\theta} + \tan^4{\theta}} = \dfrac{4\tan^2{\theta}+\left( 1-\tan^2{\theta}\right)^2}{ \left( 1-\tan^2{\theta}\right)^2}.]

Let's now recall the double-angle formula for tangent:

[MATH: \dfrac{2\tan{\theta}}{1-\tan^2{\theta}}=\tan{2\theta}]

Now, splitting the fraction, using the double-angle formula, and applying the tangent-secant formula, we obtain

[MATH: (4\tan^{2} θ + (1 − \tan^{2} θ)^{2})/((1 − \tan^{2} θ)^{2})|= (4\tan^{2} θ)/((1 − \tan^{2} θ)^{2}) + ((1 − \tan^{2} θ)^{2})/((1 − \tan^{2} θ)^{2}); = (4\tan^{2} θ)/((1 − \tan^{2} θ)^{2}) + ((1 − \tan^{2} θ)^{2})/((1 − \tan^{2} θ)^{2}); = ((2\tan θ)/(1 − \tan^{2} θ))^{2} + 1; = \tan^{2} 2θ + 1; = \sec^{2} 2θ.]

Therefore,

[MATH: \dfrac{4\tan^2{\theta}+\left( 1-\tan^2{\theta}\right)^2}{1 - 2\tan^2{\theta} + \tan^4{\theta}} = \sec^2{2\theta}.]
